summary: Under /EncryptMetadata false every stream whose /Type is /Metadata is read under Identity, not only the document-level metadata stream: a page's (or any component's, §14.3.2) metadata stream, encrypted under /StmF as the clause requires, is returned as its ciphertext. The writer's mirror (encrypt_for_update, and serialize's cleartext count) leaves every such stream in the clear the same way.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4.2 Table 21 /EncryptMetadata: "Indicates whether the document-level metadata stream (see 14.3.2, "Metadata streams") shall be encrypted." §7.6.4.3.2 step (f) NOTE 1: "This provision pertains only to document-level XMP metadata." Table 27 /EncryptMetadata says the same for the public-key handler.
change: Exempt only the stream the catalog's /Metadata names (the object number read from the catalog after authentication, kept beside encrypt_object); every other /Type /Metadata stream takes /StmF or its own /Crypt filter. Apply the same rule in encrypt_for_update and serialize.

A conforming V4 R4 file whose /CF carries /Identity << /Length 40 >> beside a 16-byte StdCF derives a 5-byte key and refuses its own user password. The same read takes a filter /StmF does not name; Table 20's /V 4 row states the key length outright (128 bits).

summary: A stream whose /Crypt decode parameters name a filter /CF does not define is decrypted under Identity (Encryption::named_method's unwrap_or(Method::Identity)), so its ciphertext is returned as its data with nothing said — the trap-5 outcome crypt_filters refuses for /StmF and /StrF naming an undefined filter. The clause's Identity default is for a missing /Name only. The public-key path reaches the same default through decrypt_stream when the name has no own key.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.6.6: "The stream's DecodeParms entry shall contain a Crypt filter decode parameters dictionary (see "Table 14 -Optional parameters for Crypt filters") whose Name entry specifies the particular crypt filter that shall be used (if missing, Identity is used)." Table 20 /CF: "Every crypt filter used in the document shall have an entry in this dictionary, except for the standard crypt filter names".
change: An undefined, non-standard name decrypts nothing: decrypt_stream returns None (decryption_failed, the stream refuses by itself), and encrypt_stream refuses likewise; Identity stays the answer for an absent /Name and for /Identity.

status: fixed (ADR 3233; named_method returns None for a name /CF does not define, and the stream is refused)

summary: The public-key handler's filter_lists reads every /CF entry other than the /StmF and /StrF filters as a stream filter with a recipient list of its own, /Identity included: an /Identity entry carrying /Recipients as an array refuses the whole document (UnsupportedEncryption) where the same document without it asks for a certificate; one carrying a string becomes an own key that is scanned. 2038-B07's fix made the standard handler ignore the entry; the public-key path still reads it.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.6.2 Table 20 /CF: "Any keys in the CF dictionary that are listed in "Table 26 - Standard crypt filter names" shall be ignored by a PDF processor. Instead, the PDF processor shall use properties of the respective standard crypt filters."

summary: An embedded file stream is recognised by /Type /EmbeddedFile alone, which Table 44 makes optional: an attachment without the entry is decrypted under /StmF instead of /EFF. With /EFF /Identity beside an AESV2 /StmF the untyped attachment's plaintext fails AES padding and the stream reads as nothing; the same stream with /Type stated reads correctly. The comment that RF and EF share a filter "by construction, since both are /Type /EmbeddedFile streams" rests on the same assumption.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.6.2 Table 20 /EFF: "The name of the crypt filter that shall be used when encrypting embedded file streams that do not have their own crypt filter specifier". §7.11.4 Table 44 /Type: "(Optional) The type of PDF object that this dictionary describes; if present, shall be EmbeddedFile for an embedded file stream." §7.6.6: "related files ( RF ) shall use the same crypt filter as the embedded file ( EF )".
change: Recognise an embedded file stream by the reference that makes it one: collect the object numbers /EF and /RF entries of file specifications name (lazily, the first time a stream with no /Type and no /Crypt is decrypted under an /EFF that differs from /StmF), or decrypt such a stream on demand from the file specification's side. Only files whose /EFF differs from /StmF are affected.
